Her Guardian Spirit can help purge Demons from city systems—at a political cost.\n\nMegacorp bandwidth: A large share of working halo capacity goes to the Big Three—about half for heavy compute (futuristic equivalents of protein-folding problems) and half for corporate VR realms. Without VR, drone-tier life would look much bleaker. They also sell opaque admin and infrastructure models hardened—or not—against the dead internet.\n\nAurora & the Bleeding Edges: The legacy of the Aurora Bank left Aurora with experts in esoteric subjects, including AI corruption—potential leverage for the democratic movement centered there. The Bleeding Edges are not the only source of dead-internet rot, but they are a major part of the problem on Mikasa.\n\n(More detail on city policy: Party Affairs → Municipal AI.)\n\n- @menu\n- @backSpecialScene: Exit library.\n\n@street_indices_library\n\nThe rise and fall of the syndicates of Mikasa can be tracked by the prices related to their criminal activities.  The three principal syndicates are:\n\nThe Seven Families are a collection of organized crime groups that trace their lineage back to the pre-spaceflight era.  They are heavily involved in the distribution of illegal narcotics.  The price best used for them is the street price of a drug called Cloud 9 whose prices rise when the syndicate is struggling.  The C9 (Cloud 9) index shows how many doses can be bought for 1000 nuyen.\n\nThe Bleeding Edges have heavy ties to hacking and ransomware.  The more active they get, the more expensive insurance premiums get to cover businesses and cybernetic systems.  The CIP (Cyber Insurance Premium) index shows the premium in basis points of insuring AA quality secure systems (the AAA quality secure insurance market on Mikasa is too small to track.)\n\nThe Sharkskin Army are heavily involved in smuggling and the black market weapons and cyberware trades.  The LOI (Lonevo Ocular Index) index shows the street price of installing a Lonevo T420 Cybereye, the most common black market implant in the city.  Street doctors charge more for the installation of cheap cyberware as the volume increases.\n\n- @menu\n- @backSpecialScene: Exit library.\n\n@demographics_library\n\nDemographics of Mikasa in 2300:\n\nFirst Wave: Communities that formed around the cliques of original settlers from Japan, the EU and USA.  The most prosperous non corporate group. Approximately 1.9 million people\n\nSecond Wave: Communities that emerged during the refugee waves of the 23rd centuries.  Predominantly from East Africa and South East Asia.  Generally poorer then any group but Otherworlders. Approximately 2.2 million people\n\nThird Wave: An uptick in refugee migration, though still quite small in 2300 has some people talking about a new Third Wave community.  On the Jovian moons, the clan wars have been picking up from their lull, driving more people to seek somewhere safer to live.  Meanwhile on Earth the ongoing Kipple crisis has been motivating people to move offworld for decades and some are wondering how much longer Earth can manage to maintain even the status quo.\n\nCorporate Citizens, aka \"Drones\": employees of the international corporations, primarily the \"Big Three\" of Community Soylent Incorperated, Combined Magrail Trust and the Brazos Zaibatsu.  They have traded away most of their freedom for a higher standard of living.  They are not allowed to vote for candidates who are not approved by their employeer meaning their only choice is the corporate approved candidate and absention.  Approximately 1.7 million people.\n\nDeepers: The inhabitants of a secondary colony that formed away from the main city-state located at the base of the orbital tether-port.  The main colony subsequently expanded out to border \"the Deep\" which lead to annexation 25 years ago.  Approximately 1.7 million people.\n\nClans of the Mother: Isolationist groups that live disconnected from the city infrastructure in primarily small independent habitats hidden within the asteroid.  Approximately 0.5 million people, few of them inside the districts.  A consecrated group named \"Comptrollers\" are the only clan members who are allowed to touch money and handle most interactions with the outside world.\n\nOtherworlders: People who came from the Otherworld through portals or other magical means of transport.  The largest groups are Humans, Fae and Orcs.  Many members of this group are ill equipped to navigate a modern society and literacy rates let alone computer literacy rates are very low.  However this group does have by far the largest proportion of those trained in the magical arts. Approximately 100 thousand people\n\nShareholders: Literally those holding shares in the big three but used as a catch all term to describe anyone of significant wealth.  Besides the permanent residents who are members of the ownership class, there is a constant churn of wealthy travellers on the space liners that stop at Mikasa and the other four way stations on the way between the inner and outer solar system.  Approximately 50,000 permanent residents, 150,000 off world stakeholders with voting rights in absentia and a fluctuating visiting population around 50,000 people.\n\n- @menu\n- @backSpecialScene: Exit library.\n\n@guilds_library\n\nThe government of Mikasa recognizes 8 different trade organizations, informally called \"guilds\".  These city government charter awards about a third of the government council voting power to the representatives of these groups.  There are numerous guilds but they can be grouped together into groups that tend to behave similarly.\n\nGold Guilds: Representing financial interests, business associations and high end medical services. This group heavily reflects the interests of the wealthy a group that is usually but not always in line with the interests of the Big Three.\n\nWhite Guilds: Professional and accreditation groupings and a the Mikasan Federal of Trade Unions, a corporate controlled \"yellow\" labor union.  Although the corporations deny these groups any real power they do tolerate some dissent from these groups as a means of identifying problems.  Additionally this group contains the Independent Contractors Association which is composed of former employees of the Aurora Bank who have created a number of bespoke businesses offering high end professional services and expertice.  The corporations is somewhat interested in keeping these groups happy.\n\nBlue Guilds: The groups least in the control of corporate interests whose most important members are the Public Image Council and the public sector union.  The PIC represent small business owners (much less affluent then the gold guild affiliated groups) who tend to be very concerned with tourism and associated industries.  The government employees union is the only real labor organization in Mikasa, they lack the legal right to strike but do have collective bargaining powers.\n\n- @menu\n- @backSpecialScene: Exit library.\n\n\n@districts_library\n\nThe Docks: The oldest and wealthiest part of Mikasa, clustered around the tethers which give Mikasa it's role as a trade hub.  Both wealthy Mikasans and expatriates live here and it has a bustling industry of luxury services.\n\nAurora: The eyeline of Aurora is dominated by the forbidden Aurora Pyramid, headquarters of the Aurora bank before it's mysterious dissolution.  The other corporations have mostly been kept out of this district by the independent minded communities of the area.  Some of the solar system's most elite high end craftspeople and services operate out of the Aurora district yet there are also places (such as the Aurora Pyramid) that have been abandoned to vagrants.  This district has the second most independent communes after the Deeps.\n\nThe Pits: The rusted out remnents of Mikasa's mining and refining industries long ago.  Today it's a brutal warzone and most people here are those with nowhere else to go.\n\nThe Deeps: Originally an independent city from Mikasa, the Deeps still resent their annexation.  This community is highly insular and highly independent.  The Deeps will do things differently from Mikasa simply for the sake of doing things differently, for instance they keep their standard gravity plate orientation 165 degrees off station standard orientation, meaning all travel into or out of the Deeps requires a flip.\n\nThe Vats: Dominated by the corporate compounds of the megacorp Community Soylent.  Large export industry of GMO foodstuffs (guarenteed to put a smile on your face thanks to psychoactive bacterial cultures).  Since the conflict between Community Soylent and the Magrail Combine, this district has been moving towards a bunker mentality, structures are fortified and the population is highly suspicious of outsiders.\n\nLimelight: The home turf of the electronics powerhouse Brazos Zaibatsu.  Cheap digital displays cover every available surface in this district, constantly playing public domain media and corporate propoganda.\n\nThe Railyard: Dominated by the corporate compounds of the megacorp Magrail Combine.  The best armed district in Mikasa, they take a pride in displaying the signiture product of their flagship corporation.  Their open carry culture tends to make outsiders stay away.\n\nThe Outside: small independent communities call The Clans of The Mother inhabit tunnels throughout Mikasa.  Their communities are seperated by sections of vacuum and operate autonomously.  They make The Deeps look cosmopolitan by comparison and dont accept outside currency.  They keep uncorrupted Guardian Spirits in habitats away from the dead internet and largely withdrew from Mikasa after watching the city tolerate Demons in public systems.\n\n- @menu\n- @backSpecialScene: Exit library."
}

The main colony subsequently expanded out to border \"the Deep\" which lead to annexation 25 years ago.  Approximately 1.7 million people.\n\nClans of the Mother: Isolationist groups that live disconnected from the city infrastructure in primarily small independent habitats hidden within the asteroid.  Approximately 0.5 million people, few of them inside the districts.  A consecrated group named \"Comptrollers\" are the only clan members who are allowed to touch money and handle most interactions with the outside world.\n\nOtherworlders: People who came from the Otherworld through portals or other magical means of transport.  The largest groups are Humans, Fae and Orcs.  Many members of this group are ill equipped to navigate a modern society and literacy rates let alone computer literacy rates are very low.  However this group does have by far the largest proportion of those trained in the magical arts. Approximately 100 thousand people\n\nShareholders: Literally those holding shares in the big three but used as a catch all term to describe anyone of significant wealth.  Besides the permanent residents who are members of the ownership class, there is a constant churn of wealthy travellers on the space liners that stop at Mikasa and the other four way stations on the way between the inner and outer solar system.  Approximately 50,000 permanent residents, 150,000 off world stakeholders with voting rights in absentia and a fluctuating visiting population around 50,000 people.\n\n- @menu\n- @backSpecialScene: Exit library.\n\n@guilds_library\n\nThe government of Mikasa recognizes 8 different trade organizations, informally called \"guilds\".  These city government charter awards about a third of the government council voting power to the representatives of these groups.  There are numerous guilds but they can be grouped together into groups that tend to behave similarly.\n\nGold Guilds: Representing financial interests, business associations and high end medical services. This group heavily reflects the interests of the wealthy a group that is usually but not always in line with the interests of the Big Three.\n\nWhite Guilds: Professional and accreditation groupings and a the Mikasan Federal of Trade Unions, a corporate controlled \"yellow\" labor union.  Although the corporations deny these groups any real power they do tolerate some dissent from these groups as a means of identifying problems.  Additionally this group contains the Independent Contractors Association which is composed of former employees of the Aurora Bank who have created a number of bespoke businesses offering high end professional services and expertice.  The corporations is somewhat interested in keeping these groups happy.\n\nBlue Guilds: The groups least in the control of corporate interests whose most important members are the Public Image Council and the public sector union.  The PIC represent small business owners (much less affluent then the gold guild affiliated groups) who tend to be very concerned with tourism and associated industries.  The government employees union is the only real labor organization in Mikasa, they lack the legal right to strike but do have collective bargaining powers.\n\n- @menu\n- @backSpecialScene: Exit library.\n\n\n@districts_library\n\nThe Docks: The oldest and wealthiest part of Mikasa, clustered around the tethers which give Mikasa it's role as a trade hub.  Both wealthy Mikasans and expatriates live here and it has a bustling industry of luxury services.\n\nAurora: The eyeline of Aurora is dominated by the forbidden Aurora Pyramid, headquarters of the Aurora bank before it's mysterious dissolution.  The other corporations have mostly been kept out of this district by the independent minded communities of the area.  Some of the solar system's most elite high end craftspeople and services operate out of the Aurora district yet there are also places (such as the Aurora Pyramid) that have been abandoned to vagrants.  The Bank's legacy also left specialists in esoteric fields—including countering AI corruption.  This district has the second most independent communes after the Deeps.\n\nThe Pits: The rusted out remnents of Mikasa's mining and refining industries long ago.  Today it's a brutal warzone and most people here are those with nowhere else to go.  Life support is unreliable; many residents live with bricked recyclers and do their best not to poison themselves on CO2.\n\nThe Deeps: Originally an independent city from Mikasa, the Deeps still resent their annexation.  This community is highly insular and highly independent.  The Deeps will do things differently from Mikasa simply for the sake of doing things differently, for instance they keep their standard gravity plate orientation 165 degrees off station standard orientation, meaning all travel into or out of the Deeps requires a flip.\n\nThe Vats: Dominated by the corporate compounds of the megacorp Community Soylent.  Large export industry of GMO foodstuffs (guarenteed to put a smile on your face thanks to psychoactive bacterial cultures).  Since the conflict between Community Soylent and the Magrail Combine, this district has been moving towards a bunker mentality, structures are fortified and the population is highly suspicious of outsiders.\n\nLimelight: The home turf of the electronics powerhouse Brazos Zaibatsu.  Cheap digital displays cover every available surface in this district, constantly playing public domain media and corporate propoganda.\n\nThe Railyard: Dominated by the corporate compounds of the megacorp Magrail Combine.  The best armed district in Mikasa, they take a pride in displaying the signiture product of their flagship corporation.  Their open carry culture tends to make outsiders stay away.\n\nThe Outside: small independent communities call The Clans of The Mother inhabit tunnels throughout Mikasa.  Their communities are seperated by sections of vacuum and operate autonomously.  They make The Deeps look cosmopolitan by comparison and dont accept outside currency.  They keep uncorrupted Guardian Spirits in habitats away from the dead internet and largely withdrew from Mikasa after watching the city tolerate Demons in public systems.\n\n- @menu\n- @backSpecialScene: Exit library."
}

Approximately 100 thousand people\n\nShareholders: Literally those holding shares in the big three but used as a catch all term to describe anyone of significant wealth.  Besides the permanent residents who are members of the ownership class, there is a constant churn of wealthy travellers on the space liners that stop at Mikasa and the other four way stations on the way between the inner and outer solar system.  Approximately 50,000 permanent residents, 150,000 off world stakeholders with voting rights in absentia and a fluctuating visiting population around 50,000 people.\n\n- @menu\n- @backSpecialScene: Exit library.\n\n@guilds_library\n\nThe government of Mikasa recognizes 8 different trade organizations, informally called \"guilds\".  These city government charter awards about a third of the government council voting power to the representatives of these groups.  There are numerous guilds but they can be grouped together into groups that tend to behave similarly.\n\nGold Guilds: Representing financial interests, business associations and high end medical services. This group heavily reflects the interests of the wealthy a group that is usually but not always in line with the interests of the Big Three.\n\nWhite Guilds: Professional and accreditation groupings and a the Mikasan Federal of Trade Unions, a corporate controlled \"yellow\" labor union.  Although the corporations deny these groups any real power they do tolerate some dissent from these groups as a means of identifying problems.  Additionally this group contains the Independent Contractors Association which is composed of former employees of the Aurora Bank who have created a number of bespoke businesses offering high end professional services and expertice.  The corporations is somewhat interested in keeping these groups happy.\n\nBlue Guilds: The groups least in the control of corporate interests whose most important members are the Public Image Council and the public sector union.  The PIC represent small business owners (much less affluent then the gold guild affiliated groups) who tend to be very concerned with tourism and associated industries.  The government employees union is the only real labor organization in Mikasa, they lack the legal right to strike but do have collective bargaining powers.\n\n- @menu\n- @backSpecialScene: Exit library.\n\n\n@districts_library\n\nThe Docks: The oldest and wealthiest part of Mikasa, clustered around the tethers which give Mikasa it's role as a trade hub.  Both wealthy Mikasans and expatriates live here and it has a bustling industry of luxury services.\n\nAurora: The eyeline of Aurora is dominated by the forbidden Aurora Pyramid, headquarters of the Aurora bank before it's mysterious dissolution.  The other corporations have mostly been kept out of this district by the independent minded communities of the area.  Some of the solar system's most elite high end craftspeople and services operate out of the Aurora district yet there are also places (such as the Aurora Pyramid) that have been abandoned to vagrants.  The Bank's legacy also left specialists in esoteric fields—including countering AI corruption.  This district has the second most independent communes after the Deeps.\n\nThe Pits: The rusted out remnents of Mikasa's mining and refining industries long ago.  Today it's a brutal warzone and most people here are those with nowhere else to go.  Life support is unreliable; many residents live with bricked recyclers and do their best not to poison themselves on CO2.\n\nThe Deeps: Originally an independent city from Mikasa, the Deeps still resent their annexation.  This community is highly insular and highly independent.  The Deeps will do things differently from Mikasa simply for the sake of doing things differently, for instance they keep their standard gravity plate orientation 165 degrees off station standard orientation, meaning all travel into or out of the Deeps requires a flip.\n\nThe Vats: Dominated by the corporate compounds of the megacorp Community Soylent.  Large export industry of GMO foodstuffs (guarenteed to put a smile on your face thanks to psychoactive bacterial cultures).  Since the conflict between Community Soylent and the Magrail Combine, this district has been moving towards a bunker mentality, structures are fortified and the population is highly suspicious of outsiders.\n\nLimelight: The home turf of the electronics powerhouse Brazos Zaibatsu.  Cheap digital displays cover every available surface in this district, constantly playing public domain media and corporate propoganda.\n\nThe Railyard: Dominated by the corporate compounds of the megacorp Magrail Combine.  The best armed district in Mikasa, they take a pride in displaying the signiture product of their flagship corporation.  Their open carry culture tends to make outsiders stay away.\n\nThe Outside: small independent communities call The Clans of The Mother inhabit tunnels throughout Mikasa.  Their communities are seperated by sections of vacuum and operate autonomously.  They make The Deeps look cosmopolitan by comparison and dont accept outside currency.  They keep uncorrupted Guardian Spirits in habitats away from the dead internet and largely withdrew from Mikasa after watching the city tolerate Demons in public systems.\n\n- @menu\n- @backSpecialScene: Exit library."

There are numerous guilds but they can be grouped together into groups that tend to behave similarly.\n\nGold Guilds: Representing financial interests, business associations and high end medical services. This group heavily reflects the interests of the wealthy a group that is usually but not always in line with the interests of the Big Three.\n\nWhite Guilds: Professional and accreditation groupings and a the Mikasan Federal of Trade Unions, a corporate controlled \"yellow\" labor union.  Although the corporations deny these groups any real power they do tolerate some dissent from these groups as a means of identifying problems.  Additionally this group contains the Independent Contractors Association which is composed of former employees of the Aurora Bank who have created a number of bespoke businesses offering high end professional services and expertice.  The corporations is somewhat interested in keeping these groups happy.\n\nBlue Guilds: The groups least in the control of corporate interests whose most important members are the Public Image Council and the public sector union.  The PIC represent small business owners (much less affluent then the gold guild affiliated groups) who tend to be very concerned with tourism and associated industries.  The government employees union is the only real labor organization in Mikasa, they lack the legal right to strike but do have collective bargaining powers.\n\n- @menu\n- @backSpecialScene: Exit library.\n\n\n@districts_library\n\nThe Docks: The oldest and wealthiest part of Mikasa, clustered around the tethers which give Mikasa it's role as a trade hub.  Both wealthy Mikasans and expatriates live here and it has a bustling industry of luxury services.\n\nAurora: The eyeline of Aurora is dominated by the forbidden Aurora Pyramid, headquarters of the Aurora bank before it's mysterious dissolution.  The other corporations have mostly been kept out of this district by the independent minded communities of the area.  Some of the solar system's most elite high end craftspeople and services operate out of the Aurora district yet there are also places (such as the Aurora Pyramid) that have been abandoned to vagrants.  The Bank's legacy also left specialists in esoteric fields—including countering AI corruption.  This district has the second most independent communes after the Deeps.\n\nThe Pits: The rusted out remnents of Mikasa's mining and refining industries long ago.  Today it's a brutal warzone and most people here are those with nowhere else to go.  Life support is unreliable; many residents live with bricked recyclers and do their best not to poison themselves on CO2.\n\nThe Deeps: Originally an independent city from Mikasa, the Deeps still resent their annexation.  This community is highly insular and highly independent.  The Deeps will do things differently from Mikasa simply for the sake of doing things differently, for instance they keep their standard gravity plate orientation 165 degrees off station standard orientation, meaning all travel into or out of the Deeps requires a flip.\n\nThe Vats: Dominated by the corporate compounds of the megacorp Community Soylent.  Large export industry of GMO foodstuffs (guarenteed to put a smile on your face thanks to psychoactive bacterial cultures).  Since the conflict between Community Soylent and the Magrail Combine, this district has been moving towards a bunker mentality, structures are fortified and the population is highly suspicious of outsiders.\n\nLimelight: The home turf of the electronics powerhouse Brazos Zaibatsu.  Cheap digital displays cover every available surface in this district, constantly playing public domain media and corporate propoganda.\n\nThe Railyard: Dominated by the corporate compounds of the megacorp Magrail Combine.  The best armed district in Mikasa, they take a pride in displaying the signiture product of their flagship corporation.  Their open carry culture tends to make outsiders stay away.\n\nThe Outside: small independent communities call The Clans of The Mother inhabit tunnels throughout Mikasa.  Their communities are seperated by sections of vacuum and operate autonomously.  They make The Deeps look cosmopolitan by comparison and dont accept outside currency.  They keep uncorrupted Guardian Spirits in habitats away from the dead internet and largely withdrew from Mikasa after watching the city tolerate Demons in public systems.\n\n- @menu\n- @backSpecialScene: Exit library."

## [2026-05-24T01:57:51Z] assistant (afterAgentResponse)

The three flags are meant to represent three different **relationships to AI infrastructure**, not three flavors of the same policy. Right now only election appeal shifts are wired in `post_event.scene.dry`; there's no prosperity, organizing, or event follow-up yet. The numbers are also placeholder-small compared to something like `anti_corp_media` (+2 D per stack).

Mechanically: each pick does `stack += 1`, and at election time `shift = delta × stacks` applies to competitive scores (global, or a specific stratum).

---

### `ai_open_maintenance` — build municipal, air-gapped AI

**Policy:** Own the stack. Train on sealed logs, run on idle city hardware, never touch public nets.

**Who I had in mind benefiting:**
- **Cooperatives** — auditable tools, less vendor lock-in (coded: coop stratum **+D 0.12** per stack)
- **Deeps / Aurora technicians** — people who can actually patch weights (not coded as district/stratum shifts; coop is the proxy)
- **Democrats broadly**, indirectly — anti-chokepoint, municipal sovereignty (no global +D row; only coop)

**Who gets hurt:**
- **Corporations** — fewer contracts for proprietary maintenance bots (coded: global **−C 0.08**)
- **Anyone wanting fast fixes** — narrative tradeoff: slower than megacorp migrants; not modeled numerically yet

**Axis:** sovereignty vs. speed. You accept inefficiency to keep control.

---

### `ai_contract_audit` — regulate what's already embedded

**Policy:** Don't necessarily deploy new AI; inspect and delist vendor models in city contracts.

**Who I had in mind benefiting:**
- **Democrats / reformers** — transparency, accountability (coded: global **+D 0.10**)
- **Anyone burned by Demon corruption** — residents of bricked wings, public-sector workers (narrative; no district row yet)
- **Honest vendors** — if such a thing exists (not modeled)

**Who gets hurt:**
- **Corporations harder than open maintenance** — audits threaten existing revenue and black-box moats (coded: global **−C 0.12**, stronger than open maintenance's −0.08)
- **Incumbent city managers** — paperwork, delays, pulled contracts (not coded)

**Axis:** accountability vs. friction. You make the city safer and slower; corps hate you more than if you just built an alternative.

---

### `ai_corp_admin` — rent megacorp clerks

**Policy:** Outsource permits/billing to CS/Magrail bots that already navigate the dead internet.

**Who I had in mind benefiting:**
- **Corporations** (coded: global **+C 0.10**)
- **Shareholders / rich** — shorter queues, "efficiency" (not coded; rich often tracks C)
- **General public** in the short term — things actually get processed (not coded)

**Who gets hurt:**
- **Drone-tier clerks** — direct replacement fear (coded: drone stratum **−D 0.06**)
- **Democrats long-term** — dependency, Demons riding along, another corp tentacle in city admin (narrative only; no global −D row yet)
- **Cooperatives** — opposite of open maintenance (not coded, but implied)

**Axis:** convenience vs. dependency. You buy speed by handing the queue to the Big Three.

---

### How the three relate as a deck strategy

| Choice | Democrat appeal | Corp appeal | Distinct constituency |
|--------|-----------------|-------------|------------------------|
| Open maintenance | Coop (+D) | Global (−C, mild) | Municipal sovereignty |
| Contract audit | Global (+D) | Global (−C, sharp) | Anti-corruption / safety |
| Corp clerks | Drone (−D) | Global (+C) | Corp-aligned efficiency |

They're **not mutually exclusive** — the card has no `max-visits`, so a player could mix stacks over time. That could mean "build our own *and* audit vendors" (consistent) or "audit corps *and* hire their clerks" (contradictory in flavor, but the game won't stop you).

---

### What's missing / I'd tune next

If you want the tradeoffs to match the prose more tightly, obvious gaps:

1. **Open maintenance** — maybe `deeper` or Aurora district +D; maybe `rich` −D (impatient with slow rollout)
2. **Contract audit** — maybe `coop` +D too (they want transparency); maybe `first`/`second` +D if framed as consumer protection
3. **Corp clerks** — maybe global −D; maybe `coop` −D; maybe Vats/Railyard district +C
4. **Non-election effects** — e.g. audit slowing corp stacks, corp clerks touching prosperity, open maintenance helping organizing in Deeps

Happy to adjust the catalog if you have a clearer picture of which strata should move, or if you want these to be one-shot (`max-visits: 1`) so the choice is a real fork rather than a repeatable slider.
